pr_title: Fix multiple issues with one-way collisions
pr_body:
This is a salvage of #36280, because, despite the original author's [decision](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/36280#issuecomment-702923451) to close #36280 in favour of #38471, #38471 does not solve all the issues that were solved by #36280.

This PR does a few things:
- For RigidBodies, uses the collision normal determined by relative motion to determine whether or not a one-way collision has occurred.
- For KinematicBodies, performs additional checks to ensure a one-way collision has occurred, and averages the recovery step over all collision shapes.

I have made some slight changes to the original PR to minimise the necessary changes and make this PR easy to review. I have also made the original author a co-author of the commit.

I have tested and confirmed that this PR fixes the following issues:
Fixes #25732
Fixes #25967
Fixes #28794
Fixes #34242
Fixes #35776
Fixes #40006
Fixes #42175
Fixes #43266

Note: #36280 claimed to fix other issues too. However, I found that several of these issues were already fixed (so I have updated them accordingly), or are actually not fixed by this PR.

**Edit:** Updated to remove the change that caused the bug [reported](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/42574#issuecomment-711069694) by @Rhathe.

**Edit:** Updated to fix the bugs identified by @Rhathe [here](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/42574#issuecomment-715392217) and [here](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/42574#issuecomment-716117102).

**Edit:** Updated to fix #43266, which is the same bug identified by @AttackButton [here](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/42574#issuecomment-719957095).

@capnm The `RigidBody` is not moving perfectly horizontally. It's actually rocking slightly, which is why you see the contact points flickering. This will result in slightly different collisions due to slightly different starting conditions. With the original example project, the collision normal is `<-1, 0.000295927>` i.e. pointing slightly upwards; so it's stopped. In your example project, the collision normal is `<-1, -0.000422864>` i.e. pointing slightly downwards; so it's allowed through. Setting the `RigidBody` to `Character` mode, prevents rotations i.e. the rocking and the collision normal is `<-1, 0>`, which is stopped as with the `KinematicBody`

Note: `RigidBody` one-way collisions are only checked at the time of collision. The `RigidBody` is then either allowed or disallowed to pass through until it exits the one-way collision body. This results in the differences seen around the edge case of a perpendicular collision.

I'd say it's the RigidBody2D behavior that needs to be fixed instead of the KinematicBody2D's behavior. That collision check is for if the collision vector is perpendicular to the one way vector, so it results in colliding with the side if your character jumps and falls to the side of a one way platform. I uploaded another version of the test code to show that, this time with both bodies being KinematicBody2Ds. I also show that the bug still shows up if the ground platform is tilted by -1 degrees.

In response to @akien-mga [comment](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/42574#issuecomment-712850139), to help validate this PR, I've created [Godot Gym](https://github.com/madmiraal/godot-gym) with three initial tests based on the three key issues:
1. **Swimming Pool Tests:** Contains 24 tests. It's based on the [updated MRP](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/25732#issuecomment-466669002) from @DleanJeans in the reopened #25732.
2. **Block Climb Test:** This is an exaggeration of the `TileMap` issue raised by @bemyak [above](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/42574#issuecomment-711318352) i.e. that collisions with the side of a one-way collision object should be treated as pass through. I think @Rhathe disagrees with this view from his comment [here](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/42916#issuecomment-712936847).
3. **Corner Grip Tests:** Contains 60 automated tests. This should test all the corner cases. I believe the corner cases should be treated as: "Should never collide unless: the direction is downward and it doesn't hit the side first." Again, I think @Rhathe disagrees with this view from his comment [here](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/42916#issuecomment-712956424). Note: Some of the failure cases are not limited to one-way collisions and are related to #23140 i.e. `KinematicBody` zero pixel overlap collisions.

Note: This PR fixes the issues tested in test 1: Swimming Pool Tests and 2: Block Climb Test (assuming @Rhathe agrees). It does not address the corner cases identified in test 3: Corner Grip Tests. In fact the results suggest it now fails two more; so that will need to be investigated to see whether or not this PR would cause a noticeable regression.

I've done some digging, and I've found some interesting things. First, the Corner Grip Tests confirms that this PR fixes a number of issues:
1. A `KinematicBody` no longer catches the corner when coming from below a one-way platform i.e. resolves #25967.
2. A `KinematicBody` no longer misses the corner when coming from above.
3. A `RigidBody` no longer collides with the sides of one-way shapes.

This accounts for 5 of the 16 failed tests reported by the Corner Grip Tests under 3.2.3.stable. Another 9 are due to other, non-one-way specific issues e.g. #23140. The remaining 2 are borderline cases: two corners colliding (could be treated as either the top or the side) or colliding with the side when moving perpendicular to the side.

Second, the Corner Grip Tests with this PR have exposed an issue with the `RigidBody` collision solver. See #43014. The Corner Grip Tests report 7 new failures when run against this PR due to this issue. However, this is an existing issue that has been exposed by these tests, not a regression caused by this PR.

In addition, the Corner Grip Tests have revealed an additional problem with `KinematicBodies` glancing the corner of a normal `CollisionShape` too. See #43012 .

I thought so too, but:
1. The [issue](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/42574#issuecomment-719957095) identified by @AttackButton is actually due to the collision solver reporting a collision when the overlap is negative (a separate bug that I haven't had time to create an issue for yet due to the difficulty in creating an MRP). The update is a workaround to ignore small overlaps (positive or negative) as they (so far) only reveal themselves during later unsticking steps i.e. when the overlap is supposed to be zero.
2. Whether or not to ignore a one-way `CollisionShape` is calculated during the unsticking phase. It basically decides whether or not it is already inside the `CollisionShape`. Here the `valid_depth` parameter is relevant, because it needs to account for moving platforms. However, when colliding with the object for the first time, we don't want this work around to apply, because, when extracting collision information, the overlap is deliberately small and we don't want it to be ignored because it is small.

The issue identified [above](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/42574#issuecomment-720806240) is both related to point 2 and #16414 (see [comment](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/16414#issuecomment-687757743)). When determining the safe and unsafe distance to travel, it is actually colliding with the left-hand shape; instead of ignoring it as a one-way collision object, because the overlap is too small i.e. point 2. Then, when attempting to extract the collision information, it ignores it, because the overlap is too small. This happens whether or not the right-hand shape is a one-way collision or not i.e. #16414.

It is not visible when the right-hand shape is not a one-way shape, because `move_and_slide()` is called again in the next physics iteration. When the shape is not a one-way shape, the unsticking part of the algorithm pushes it up. When it is a one-way shape, it is deemed to already be inside the shape and so it's ignored. This problem is revealed by only performing one `move_and_slide()` step.

Finally, it's worth pointing out that the issue identified [above](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/42574#issuecomment-720806240) requires the overlap between the `KinematicBody2D` and the left-hand `StaticBody2D` to be less than 0.003. i.e. this issue is not seen if the initial x-position of the `KinematicBody2D` was not 631.999, but 632 (or anything less than equal to 631.996).

Updated to ensure the work around applied in the previous update only applies during the unsticking phase i.e. fixes the bug identified [above](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/42574#issuecomment-720806240).

My requirement for merging this PR has not changed, we need a proper test suite for all expected behaviors, make sure community agrees to it and have it to check for regressions.

@reduz Your requirement will never be met, because it cannot be met. It is neither quantified ("make sure community agrees to it") nor constrained ("all expected behaviors").

While I agree that testing is important, and an open [test suite](https://github.com/madmiraal/godot-gym) is useful, it will never be able to guarantee there will not be regressions (only reduce the likelihood). Programming is hard, physics programming especially so, but the strength of open source software is many contributors providing incremental improvements over time. Putting unrealistic demands on contributors and not providing constructive feedback will only alienate them and result in [numerous](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aopen+label%3Atopic%3Aphysics), [serious](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aopen+label%3Atopic%3Aphysics+label%3Acrash) [problems](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/35780) and [regressions](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/35713) [not being addressed](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/570) for [years](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/2092) despite [numerous](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+label%3Atopic%3Aphysics) submitted [fixes](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/35945); including this one.

The only thing which I'm not sure yet is https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/42574#issuecomment-729754425 which seems to be a pre-existing bug that this PR aggravates?

Physics in Godot has been bad for years. This PR provides a lot of major improvements and fixes a lot of issues in my projects, IMO Godot really really needs this.

> The only thing which I'm not sure yet is #42574 (comment) which seems to be a pre-existing bug that this PR aggravates? This PR doesn't address existing issues with rotated objects e.g. #25313, because there is a bigger problem with rotated objects as rotating the platform (red box) a bit more shows:
3.2.3.stable ![42574i 2 3 2 3](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/9253928/100538383-5b314100-3227-11eb-911d-525dabd16e11.gif) With #42574 ![42574i 2 fixed](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/9253928/100538391-66846c80-3227-11eb-960f-36d1a664d6e2.gif)
With this PR (#42574) the behaviour appears correct. However, a few more rotations will reveal the complexity of the problem. First lets rotate the scene, so that the platform is not rotated:
3.2.3.stable ![42574i 4 3 2 3](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/9253928/100538544-54ef9480-3228-11eb-9faf-d7e5f2f28ec9.gif) With #42574 ![42574i 4 fixed](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/9253928/100538560-6173ed00-3228-11eb-8917-b928817e3197.gif)
With this PR (#42574) the behaviour still appears correct. However, if we now un-rotate the player:
3.2.3.stable ![42574i 5 3 2 3](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/9253928/100538676-20c8a380-3229-11eb-9692-3dd1150baa9c.gif) With #42574 ![42574i 5 fixed](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/9253928/100538697-39d15480-3229-11eb-8c8e-dcf5f0141dbd.gif)
The behaviour with this PR (#42574) changes, but, not only is it consistent with the current behaviour, it is the required, correct behaviour to ensure bodies, with simulated gravity, don't get caught inside adjacent one-way platforms. See the explanation [above](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/42574#issuecomment-711318352). Therefore, I think, as [suggested](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/42574#issuecomment-725973734) by @akien-mga prior to this separate, pre-existing issue being raised, that "this has reached a pretty good status to be merged now, and any potential regressions could be handled in follow up PRs."; including discussing the appropriate behaviour with rotated platforms and bodies.

> The only thing which I'm not sure yet is #42574 (comment) which seems to be a pre-existing bug that this PR aggravates?

The pre-existing bug had to deal with hugging the platform when colliding with corners. This bug deals with 90 degree rotated objects colliding on the bottom.

> This PR doesn't address existing issues with rotated objects e.g. #25313, because there is a bigger problem with rotated objects as rotating the platform (red box) a bit more shows:

#25313 doesn't actually deal with rotated objects. Take the minimum project from there, remove the 90 degree shape rotation, move the static bodies to the side, and give the kinematic body a horizontal velocity, and you will see the same issue. The actual problem there is that the testing kinematic body doesn't take its own one way collision into account when colliding with objects, only the other objects' one way collision.

Your cases don't really deal with rotated bodies either, as you can get the same results from having a diamond shaped object.

| 3.2.3 stable  | current PR |
| --- | --- |
| ![stable](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1882199/100554919-4a53f000-3266-11eb-8322-6452b422bec3.gif) | ![pr](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1882199/100554925-52ac2b00-3266-11eb-9276-8f71e4a296ef.gif) |

[test_move_one_way_diamond.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/5612930/test_move_one_way_diamond.zip)

Having 90 degree rotated objects not working correctly is a significant regression, as the only way to have something like [one-way walls/doors](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/20204) is to [rotate it by 90 degrees](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/12791#issuecomment-343350675), as you cannot specify one way collision direction, and is essential if you want one way directions in a [top-down game](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/18493). While for many rotations it seems this PR has better behavior than the current version, 90 degree rotations are an arguably more important use case and this PR would necessarily have to reopen those past issues.
